C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.Summary: Make "this deal is cancelled" a real identity check on every asynchronous answer of the search-and-workspace zone, closing the Wave-3 bundle-2 criterion «при очистке/отмене/смене запроса прежний ответ отбрасывается» (when the query is cleared, cancelled or replaced, the previous answer is discarded): the project-search store claims its generation on every runSearch path so clearing the keyword can no longer resurrect stale matches, the unreachable didSearchPaths limits (100 in the store, 30 in quick open — the wire event they wait for does not exist) are replaced by an honest delivered-match cap in the #303 partial voice, closing the command palette cancels the in-flight quick-open walk and the palette drops superseded search resolutions by request identity, the muya image path hints get the same sequence guard the link picker already has, and a folder close that races the watcher subscription can no longer leak the renderer listener.
C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the green-search2 worktree (branch spec/search-lifecycle-discard, base 689df8aa); source findings are WAVE3-SCOUT-SEARCH (2026-11-22, the 2026-11-22 wave-3 search scout record) keys SEARCH-STALE-COMPLETION (3), SEARCH-LIMIT-UNREACHABLE (5), the quick-open remnants of key 4, PATH-STALE-HINTS image flavor (14) and FOLDER-CLOSE-LISTENER (15). One root: a real cancellation-identity mechanism exists only in the search store (the monotonic _searchGeneration); searcher consumers, the command palette, the muya image selector and the watcher subscription all decide cancellation ad hoc, by flags, without an identity check. store/search.js claims the generation only at the real spawn ("const generation = ++this._searchGeneration", :178), so the early returns bypass the guard: clearing the query ("if (!this.keyword) { this.results = []; this.running = false; return }", :153-157) and the cancel line ("if (this.running && activeCancel) activeCancel()", :149) leave the generation untouched; the cancelled searcher settles with resolve (outerPromise.cancel sends mt::search-cancel and settles, src/renderer/src/node/ripgrepSearcher.js:110-113), and the stale completion's guard ("if (generation !== this._searchGeneration)", :220) passes and writes the outdated collected set over the just-cleared results — after the user empties the input, the old matches visibly come back. Limits: the events the two limit branches wait for do not exist — the backend emits only kind match/complete/cancelled/error (SearchEvent) and the window shim's mt::search-event translation branch handles exactly those kinds with no searchedPaths case (src/renderer/src/_shims/install-window-globals.js:395-427), so the store's "didSearchPaths: (n) => { if (!canceled && n > 100) { canceled = true; if (searchPromise.cancel) searchPromise.cancel(); this.error = `Showing first 100 results only` } }" (:196-202) and quickOpen's "didSearchPaths: (numPathsFound) => { if (!canceled && numPathsFound > 30) { canceled = true; if (promises.cancel) { promises.cancel() } }" (src/renderer/src/commands/quickOpen.js:139-147, comment "Cancel when more than 30 files were found. User should specify the search query.") are dead code: there is no result cap at all today, the only string promising one is unreachable, and the store test pinning it lives entirely on a mock ("canceling on >100 paths sets error message", tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts:228-261). That hardcoded English string also sits in this.error — the failure voice #303 defined — so even if it fired it would render as "Search failed". Quick open: "unload = () => { this.subcommands = [] }" (:78-80) clears the list but does not cancel an in-flight walk, although the palette's close path calls it (handleDialogClose, src/renderer/src/components/commandPalette/index.vue:121-130); and updateCommands writes without query identity — "currentCommand.value.search(queryString).then((result) => { searcherBusy.value = false; availableCommands.value = result || []; selectedCommandIndex.value = ... })" (:215-238) — so a superseded traversal A that resolves before B briefly flashes A's partial list in the palette. Muya: the image flavor of the path autocomplete has no race guard — handleKeyUp awaits "this.muya.options.imagePathAutoComplete(value)" and dispatches "eventCenter.dispatch('muya-image-picker', { reference, list, cb })" (src/muya/lib/ui/imageSelector/index.js:168-174), so a late answer to older input overwrites the hint list; the link flavor already fixed the same defect with a sequence guard ("const seq = ++this._seq" / "// A newer keystroke won the race — drop the stale list." / "if (seq !== this._seq) return", src/muya/lib/ui/linkPathPicker/index.js:151-158). Workspace: the watcher subscription is asynchronous — "ipcWatch.subscribe(canonical, ..., { listener: { manual: true } }).then((dispose) => { watchDisposers.set(canonical, dispose) })" (src/renderer/src/store/project.js:385-396) — while CLOSE_PROJECT disposes only what is already stored ("const dispose = watchDisposers.get(canonical); if (dispose) { dispose(); watchDisposers.delete(canonical) }", :816-824); a close arriving before subscribe resolves reaches no disposer, the late .then then stores a disposer for an already-closed root that nobody will ever call, and on re-open of the same folder the stale entry and the fresh subscription overwrite each other in the map — the renderer-side listener leaks for good (the backend unwatch side, mt_close_project_root, is separate and not renderer-owned).
C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.Relationship: Direct successor of C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION (merged as #289) and C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY (merged as #303, status applied). #289's SearchSessionCoordinator keeps sole ownership of the session-wide seq and the single terminal — this change makes no backend edits at all, so that ownership is untouched by construction. #303's honest voice is reused, not weakened: its raw-promise activeCancel seam, its quiet-cancel semantics, its partialResults state and the existing localized notice (sideBar.search.resultsPartial, "Partial results — the search stopped early.", static/locales/en.json:1755) become the delivery vehicle for the honest cap; the dead English promise "Showing first 100 results only" is removed — it wrote into this.error, the failure voice, and never fired anyway — so #303's meaning of error (failures only, localized line sideBar.search.searchFailed) is restored, not diluted. Landed ON TOP of the sibling C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT (PR #320, authored in the green-search1 worktree, approved): #320 edits src/renderer/src/commands/quickOpen.js (didMatch envelope normalization only), src/renderer/src/_shims/install-window-globals.js (honest range form in the mt::search-event branch) and the projectSearch/searchResultItem keyboard surfaces — none of which this change writes; the one shared file, quickOpen.js, is edited here in disjoint regions (unload and the didSearchPaths key inside the search options object, not the didMatch consumer), and both changes keep the grouped "filePath" plus "matches" renderer envelope intact, so #320's string-id pins keep working unchanged. The plan must rebase onto #320's delivery state and rerun its suites. Sibling bundles from the same scout stay NonGoals and separable: C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE (files mode still spawns a content search; the files-mode cost and limit design — including any successor of the removed ">30 files" branch — belongs there) and C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY (case, gitignore, UTF-8, tree cost). Recorded dead-parallel, read-only, not absorbed: node/ripgrepSearcher.js keeps its dormant 'searchedPaths' dispatch case ("case 'searchedPaths': try { didSearchPaths(msg.payload) } catch {}", :66-68 — the wire never delivers it) and the typed facade src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/search.ts keeps its synthetic didSearchPaths with zero production importers. Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: Every runSearch path supersedes prior generations: the generation claim moves ahead of the early returns (one claim per runSearch invocation), so after runSearch returns early — no opened roots, empty keyword, invalid max file size — no completion belonging to a prior generation can write results, partialResults, running or activeCancel. Clearing the keyword while a search runs clears the results once and for good: the searcher's resolve-triggered .then lands on a stale generation and is dropped. The keystroke-to-keystroke guard the store already has, and #303's error/partial/cancel semantics, stay unchanged.

The unreachable wire limits are replaced by an honest delivered-match cap. The store's and quickOpen's didSearchPaths branches are deleted (the event does not exist on the wire). The project-search store caps the displayed result set on delivered matches — the sum of matches across the grouped envelopes, the same unit the overlay's summary reports — at a named constant preserving the previous promise's number (100). When the cap fires, the store cancels the in-flight walk through the existing raw-promise cancel, truncates the displayed set to the cap exactly, and marks the set partial through the existing #303 state so the overlay's existing partial notice renders; the truncation flag is set synchronously in the run's own didMatch path and never depends on the backend terminal (a UI-cancelled search settles before the terminal can deliver a partial flag). A cap is not a failure: the error state stays empty. No backend, wire or i18n change.

Quick open teardown and the palette gain identity. unload cancels the in-flight work through the existing _cancelFn seam — the pending debounce timer or the active searcher promise — while still clearing subcommands; updateCommands guards its writes with a monotonic request sequence (the linkPathPicker precedent): a resolution or rejection from a superseded request is dropped without touching availableCommands, searcherBusy or selectedCommandIndex, the newest request solely owns the list (no stale flash), and the existing silence for cancelled rejections (error.message null) is preserved.

The muya image path hints get the same race discipline as the link flavor: handleKeyUp captures a sequence number before awaiting imagePathAutoComplete and dispatches muya-image-picker only if it is still current — a late answer to older input is dropped. linkPathPicker (the precedent) and every other muya surface stay untouched.

A folder close that races the watcher subscription cannot leak the renderer listener: the subscription promise's late resolution re-checks identity before storing the disposer — if the root was closed before resolution, the late .then disposes immediately and stores nothing; a superseded subscription for the same canonical root disposes itself and never overwrites the newer disposer. CLOSE_PROJECT keeps its synchronous dispose of stored disposers and the backend unwatch.

Constraints.Constraint: No backend changes: mt_search_spawn and mt_search_cancel, the mt::search-event channel, searchId, the SearchEvent kinds (match/complete/cancelled/error), the envelope (hits/error/partial/seq) and engine selection stay untouched; no new event kind, channel or envelope field; the searchedPaths event is not introduced on the wire; src-tauri is not edited; #289's coordinator terminal ownership and #303's partial-flag wire semantics are preserved.

Generation semantics: the store's _searchGeneration stays monotonic and renderer-side; superseding is claimed once per runSearch invocation before any early return; the delivered-match cap is a same-generation honest finalization — it does not bump the generation, and its own (truncated) results plus the partial marker ride the current deal's .then; cancelRunning and the quiet-cancel behavior delivered by #303 are unchanged; the root-close defense-in-depth live-roots filter stays.

Cap specifics: counted on delivered matches (the grouped envelope's matches, summed — the unit the overlay's resultSummary reports), one named documented constant, preserving the previous promise's number (100); the displayed set is truncated to the constant exactly even when the last batch overshot; the in-flight walk is cancelled through the existing raw-promise cancel seam; the partial marker reuses the existing partialResults state and notice slot (no new copy, no new state field); no result set that hit the cap is ever presented as complete.

Quick open and palette: unload keeps its existing contract (subcommands cleared) and adds cancellation through the existing _cancelFn seam only — no new canceller machinery, no debounce or searcher changes; the palette guard is a monotonic request sequence captured at updateCommands entry (the linkPathPicker seq precedent), applied to both the .then and the .catch path; the cancelled-rejection silence (error.message null means the query was cancelled or restarted) is preserved; no palette UX redesign, no layout or ARIA changes, no placeholder or i18n changes.

Muya scope: src/muya/lib/ui/imageSelector/index.js changes only by a _seq field initialization and the identity check around the existing await/dispatch pair in handleKeyUp; the dispatch payload, the cb wiring, the link flavor (src/muya/lib/ui/linkPathPicker/index.js — the precedent) and every other muya surface are untouched; no muya public API change.

Watcher subscription: the identity re-check lives in ADD_PROJECT's subscribe .then in src/renderer/src/store/project.js (per-root monotonic subscription token plus a closed-check, or an equivalent documented identity); the pinned contract is behavioral — after CLOSE_PROJECT no renderer listener for the closed root remains subscribed, no late .then stores a disposer for a closed root, and a stale entry never overwrites a superseding subscription's disposer; the ipcWatch facade (src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/watch.ts) and the backend unwatch are read-only.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE work: no backend files-mode implementation, no wiring of the dead inclusions field, no body-read instrumentation or fixture, and no design or revival of a files-mode cap — the ">30 files" branch is removed here as dead code only, and the files-mode cost/limit question (the walk currently runs to completion on every keystroke) stays with that bundle.

No C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY work: no smart-case or gitignore-outside alignment, no UTF-8 byte-slice truncation fix, no tree-emit batching, no engine unification, no rg sidecar bundling, no search ranking or new search features.

No i18n changes (no new user-facing strings — the existing sideBar.search.resultsPartial notice carries the honest-cap voice; the removed "Showing first 100 results only" string was dead, hardcoded English), no preferences storage or schema changes, no editor find-bar changes, no linkPathPicker or link-flavor changes, no command-palette UX redesign, no changes to mt::search-event consumers outside the named files, no dependency acquisition, release version, tags or publication.

No redesign of the searcher classes and no cleanup beyond this bundle's seams: node/ripgrepSearcher.js keeps its thenable/cancel contract and its dormant 'searchedPaths' dispatch case, node/fileSearcher.js is untouched, and the dead typed facade ipc/runtime/search.ts (synthetic didSearchPaths, zero importers) stays read-only documented dead-parallel for a separate dead-code pass.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first store test — "clearing the keyword while a search is running does not bring the old matches back": with a controlled searcher mock, matches are delivered, the keyword is cleared while the search runs, the late completion resolves — and results stay empty, running stays false and activeCancel stays unset; the same discard holds for the other early-return paths (no opened roots, invalid max file size) and for a superseding keystroke. Today the stale completion rewrites the cleared results, so the test is red before the fix; the two existing generation-guard suites stay green.

Failing-first delivered-match cap test: a searcher mock delivering more than the cap in grouped envelopes ends with the displayed set truncated to the cap exactly, partialResults true (the overlay's existing partial notice renders from it), running false, the searcher's cancel invoked, and the error state untouched — a cap is not a failure; a subsequent keystroke clears the partial state; the cap fires on real didMatch deliveries, not on a synthetic path-count callback, and does not depend on the backend terminal's partial flag.

Wire-truth test: the production searcher path never delivers a searchedPaths event — the window shim's mt::search-event translation branch handles only match/complete/cancelled/error (pinned by extending tests/renderer/_shims/install-window-globals.test.js or a sibling mapping test, C-52 boot-order pins intact), and neither store/search.js nor commands/quickOpen.js passes a didSearchPaths option anymore; the replaced pins from the old mock-fed behavior are rewritten per the documented Constraint and stay named in the change record.

Failing-first quickOpen tests: unload() on an in-flight controlled search (or a pending debounce) invokes the searcher's cancel (or cancels the timer) while subcommands still clear — today it does not cancel, so the test is red before the fix; and the existing unload pins stay green. Failing-first palette stale-flash test: query A issued, query B issued, A's promise resolves first — availableCommands, selectedCommandIndex and searcherBusy are not touched by A's resolution and B's resolution solely owns the list; a stale rejection (including the message-null cancelled form) is dropped silently. Today A flashes, so the test is red before the fix.

Failing-first muya test on the image flavor: two handleKeyUp invocations with controlled imagePathAutoComplete promises — the stale resolution dispatches nothing on muya-image-picker and only the newest dispatches (payload and cb wiring unchanged); suites covering the link flavor (linkPathPicker) pass untouched.

Failing-first project-store race test on the existing ipcWatchSubscribeMock seam: CLOSE_PROJECT arrives before subscribe resolves, then the subscribe promise resolves with a spy disposer — the late .then invokes the disposer exactly once itself, the disposer map does not gain an entry for the closed root, and a re-opened root's newer disposer is never overwritten by the stale one; a subscription resolving while the root is still open stores its disposer as before; the existing C-1 subscribe/dispose suites stay green. Today the disposer leaks, so the test is red before the fix.

Graph and verification describe the final state: M-011 and M-012 SummaryDeltas plus the touched file-local contracts (store/search.js MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY; the project.js watcher-lifecycle note; the commandPalette and imageSelector notes where their maps mention the guarded paths), M-036 SummaryDelta in features.xml, V-M-011 and V-M-012 entries in verification/runtime.xml and the V-M-036 entry in verification/features.xml; all pre-existing suites — the #289 session-trace family, the #303 store/overlay/error families, searchResultItem, the quickOpen unit suites, the palette suites, the project-store suites, the shim C-52 boot-order pins and the e2e search-bar spec — pass without weakened assertions or budgets, except the two explicitly replaced dead-limit pins named in this change's record.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Named new tests pin the five behaviors: stale-clear-does-not-resurrect (a cleared or early-returned query cannot be overwritten by a prior generation), delivered-match-cap-honest-partial (truncated set, partial notice state, cancel invoked, error untouched), no-searchedpaths-on-the-wire (shim kinds plus option removal), quickopen-unload-cancels and palette-stale-request-dropped (identity guard on then and catch), image-keyup-seq-guard (stale hint list dropped), folder-close-beats-subscribe (late disposer self-disposes, no stale overwrite). Existing #289 session-trace, #303 honest-state, quickOpen, palette, project-store, searchResultItem and C-52 receipts are preserved as pre-change evidence, not relabeled; the two replaced dead-limit pins are named in the change record.

No Rust changes: no cargo command is required, and the V-M-004 receipts stay valid untouched. No new e2e: the five behaviors are cancellation-identity semantics pinned at unit and component seams — a timing-dependent stale-resolution e2e would be flaky by construction — and the existing playwright search-bar spec stays green as regression evidence. Unavailable platform or owner acceptance evidence remains explicitly open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The cap preserves the previous promise's number (100 delivered matches) as a named constant; the plan may adjust the number with documented rationale — the acceptance criterion is honesty of the notice and truncation, not the specific count. Counting delivered matches rather than traversed paths is deliberate: it is the unit the UI reports, it is identical for both engine legs, and it makes the previously unfulfillable promise executable.

The palette guard is a monotonic request sequence (the linkPathPicker precedent), not a query-string comparison: equal consecutive queries must still supersede, re-search must re-own the list, and the seq pattern is the zone canon for exactly this race.

The watcher subscription identity is implemented as a per-root monotonic subscription token plus a closed-check, or an equivalent the plan documents; the specification pins the behavioral contract (no leaked listener, no entry for a closed root, no stale overwrite), not the mechanism.

Sibling #320 (C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT) lands before this change; the plan rebases onto its delivery state and reruns its suites. The changes touch quickOpen.js in disjoint regions and this change does not modify the shim, searchResultItem or the projectSearch template, so #320's pins are unaffected by construction; if the delivery order changes, the plan re-verifies the shared-file anchor before pinning tests.
Approval of this specification does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.
